title: Lena and the Wolf
premise: Odile Kavanagh has spent twenty years as gatekeeper of Thornfell Pass, keeping the old door beneath the mountain sealed and his own past buried. When a mute child arrives speaking the dead tongue of the Undercourt, Odile learns the girl's soul was sold to the gentry below by her desperate parents—and that the debt collectors are coming to collect her body next. To save her, Odile must reopen the gate he swore to keep shut, bargain with a wolf-queen who remembers him from a life he's erased, and finally claim the name he abandoned. In the end, he wins the child back not by force but by offering the court his own forgotten soul in trade, and the two of them walk out of the mountain into a dawn where belonging is chosen, not inherited.
about_author: Emrys Okonkwo is a former border-town archivist who writes fantasy about people who live between jurisdictions and loyalties. He lives somewhere with unreliable weather and collects folk songs about doors that should never be opened.

chapters.title: The Gate That Stays Shut
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A routine winter at Thornfell Pass: checking seals, trading with smugglers, keeping everyone at arm's length. Establishes his competence, isolation, and the iron rule of the gate. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness that feels like peace but reads as fear.

chapters.title: A Knock in Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. During a blizzard, a small girl arrives barefoot, unharmed by cold, speaking a language older than any kingdom. She cannot say her name; she only draws a door. Emotional beat: dread blooming under wonder—Odile recognizes the tongue from his buried past.

chapters.title: What the Child Carries
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with a dream interlude in the girl's voice. The girl, whom he calls Wren, sleeps and her shadow moves independently. Odile realizes her soul is only half-hers—the rest is held elsewhere. Emotional beat: reluctant protectiveness hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Debt Collectors
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Three figures in fine grey clothes arrive with a contract bearing Wren's parents' signatures. They are polite, patient, and utterly certain. Odile stalls them, claiming guardianship. Emotional beat: the first open defiance of his invisible life.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Roads
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He takes Wren down the hidden paths only he knows, seeking the one person who can read the contract: Brannoc, an exiled lawyer of the Undercourt living as a village drunk. Emotional beat: fugitive urgency laced with unexpected tenderness toward the child.

chapters.title: The Lawyer in Exile
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Brannoc reads the contract and delivers the bad news: the sale is binding, the court beneath the mountain holds legal claim to Wren's soul, and debts must be paid or traded. Emotional beat: cynical pity curdling into guilt—he drafted similar contracts once.

chapters.title: Loopholes and Wolves
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. There is one precedent: a soul may be ransomed by someone the court already holds a claim on. Brannoc suspects Odile is such a man. Odile denies it violently. Emotional beat: the past knocking louder than the present threat.

chapters.title: The Name He Buried
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, framed as confession to Wren by firelight. Twenty years ago he was Odran, a tithe-child raised in the Undercourt, who escaped by selling his own name and memories to buy the door shut behind him. Emotional beat: shame transmuting into the first breath of self-forgiveness.

chapters.title: Grey Riders on the Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, rendered in her limited, strange perception. The collectors catch up; Brannoc is taken as an accomplice. Wren uses her half-soul to freeze them just long enough to flee. Emotional beat: terror and the discovery that she has power after all.

chapters.title: The Wolf-Queen's Toll
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Their escape route crosses the territory of Maelis, the wolf-queen who once was Odran's sworn friend. She demands a toll: the truth of why he left her guarding nothing. Emotional beat: grief between old friends, and Maelis agreeing to guide them—for a price deferred.

chapters.title: Descent at the Sealed Door
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They reach the gate Odile has kept shut for two decades. Opening it requires a name spoken willingly—and 'Odran' costs him physically to say. The door opens onto stairs going down forever. Emotional beat: sacrifice as threshold; no return.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Undercourt in full splendor: candlelit halls, beautiful creditors, etiquette as law. Odile presents himself as Odran returned to settle accounts. Emotional beat: vertigo of slipping back into an identity he hated.

chapters.title: Terms of Trade
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV—he has been brought below as counsel. Negotiation scenes: the court offers Wren's freedom for a new tithe of ten children from the surface. Odile refuses; the court smiles, because refusal breaches contract. Emotional beat: the trap of lawful evil.

chapters.title: The Tithe Ledger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Imprisoned in a guest-room that is also a cage, Wren finds the ledger of all sold souls—including her parents' entry, and a page with a burned-out name: Odran's. Emotional beat: understanding that adults fail children, and deciding not to accept it.

chapters.title: Maelis Comes Down
chapters.summary: Maelis's POV. The wolf-queen breaks the ancient truce by entering the court uninvited, invoking an older law: debts contracted against children under duress are void if the creditor cannot prove consent. Chaos in the hall. Emotional beat: loyalty as a weapon sharper than law.

chapters.title: Trial by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A formal hearing before the Undercourt's masked judges. Brannoc argues, Maelis testifies, the collectors counter with Wren's parents' genuine signatures. It comes down to one question: what will Odile stake? Emotional beat: rising dread as every legal avenue closes.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile stakes his own reclaimed soul—name, memories, and all—against Wren's. If he can carry his whole self out of the court without looking back, both go free; if he falters, the court keeps everything. Emotional beat: terrifying clarity; he has finally found something worth losing himself for.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Up
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, mostly Wren's. The climb through the dark as the court whispers his old life at him—his mother's voice, his childhood room, Maelis howling his name. Wren walks beside him, holding his hand, anchoring him. Emotional beat: identity as something carried together, not possessed alone.

chapters.title: Dawn at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the final step, the court shows him the one thing he cannot resist: a vision of the boy he was, still waiting below, asking why he was left. Odile answers aloud—'because I chose to live'—and steps into sunlight. Emotional beat: catharsis; the past released rather than escaped.

chapters.title: Settlements
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Aftermath: the contract dissolved, the collectors unravelling like smoke, Brannoc taking up honest practice above ground. Wren's parents arrive, penitent; Wren chooses to stay with Odile for now, visiting them in spring. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, imperfect and humane.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Door
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He rehangs the gate—not sealed this time, but locked with a key shared between him, Maelis, and Wren. He signs the pass ledger 'Odran Kavanagh' for the first time in twenty years. Emotional beat: quiet joy; belonging built rather than granted.

chapters.title: The Language of Coming Home
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Spring. Wren teaches Odile words in the old tongue; he teaches her the smugglers' roads. On the last page, she speaks her true name for the first time, and it means 'the one who was bought back.' Emotional beat: resolution as reciprocity—two saved souls making a home.
